processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials using a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
The ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h.
The homogenized ingots were hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates were cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm3 samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
The samples were solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching.
Solution-treated samples were aged at 625 °C for 3 h, followed by water quenching. The 625 °C aging condition is listed in Table 2 (625 °C aging row, 3 h column).

structures.overall_structure: After aging at 625 °C for 3 h the α (BCC) matrix of the 15Al alloy has almost completely transformed into β-Mn (the alloy was aged above 600 °C, a regime where the α matrix almost fully transforms to β-Mn within just 1 h), with abundant fine BCC and FCC Cu-rich precipitates distributed within the β-Mn.

phases_present.morphology: fine precipitates distributed within the β-Mn
fine particles located at the interfaces between the β-Mn

size.value: comparable to that of the FCC Cu-rich phase particles

precipitates.distribution: within the β-Mn / at the β-Mn interfaces
at the interfaces between the β-Mn

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α + α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase
interfaces.interface_notes: The β-Mn is poor in Cu; the fine FCC phase particles that form at the β-Mn interfaces are rich in Cu, depleted in Fe and Mn and slightly poor in Al (i.e. the FCC Cu-rich phase). EBSD revealed that the content of the FCC Cu-rich phase between β-Mn interfaces decreased gradually with increasing Al content. The TEM/interface evidence was obtained on the 15Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 6 h (its peak-hardness state).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester at a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the average of 5 measurements reported.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample repeatedly tested 5 times and hardness given by the average of 5 measurements.
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the Vickers hardness of the 15Al alloy after aging at 625 °C for 3 h (and across the full aging matrix).
characterization_methods.key_findings: 15Al aged at 625 °C for 3 h gave 889.9 ± 4.3 HV; at 625 °C and 650 °C the hardness of the 15Al alloy stabilized between 800 HV and 900 HV with prolonged aging time.

unmapped_findings: For the 15Al alloy the 625 °C aging series was essentially time-independent: 852.8 ± 24.6 HV (1 h), 889.9 ± 4.3 HV (3 h), 887.2 ± 14.1 HV (6 h) and 888.2 ± 6.6 HV (10 h) (Table 2), i.e. the 15Al hardness at 625 °C (and 650 °C) remained stabilized between 800 HV and 900 HV with prolonged aging time (b0028, b0037).

At 600 °C and above (including 625 °C), the α matrix of the 15Al alloy almost completely transformed into β-Mn within just 1 h of aging, and abundant fine BCC and FCC precipitates were observed within the β-Mn (b0052).
The peak Vickers hardness of the 15Al alloy (965.6 HV) was achieved at 600 °C for 6 h, not at the 625 °C/3 h condition of this sample (b0028, b0037, b0055).
